heading: Data access: Tac
summary: The same five annotations in the browser and on native targets. A view addresses a service, the service owns the behavior context, and the store carries the query plan.
body:
Select a language tab and copy the page, the component view and the four role files. JavaScript, TypeScript and Dart bundle for the web. Swift, Kotlin, C# and Rust stage their native hosts. Go bundles for the web as WebAssembly. The view reads {product.summary} from the service. A view can read only from a service (ADR 0030). The browser services show the order of calls. First they create the context from the Setup. Then they construct the store with it. Then they call the query and PageDefaults methods. The Dart service follows the same pattern as Yon Dart. It creates the context synchronously and constructs the store with it. The native services stay plain types, as they do elsewhere in Tac. The compiler finds their annotated entity, store and setup files and adds them to the same compile unit.

The annotations and their options are the same as in Yon. The previous section runs them in a full example. Only the realm is different. The role folders are client/entities, client/stores, client/setups and client/services (ADR 0031). Table is a modifier (an extra annotation on the entity). It does not change the entity's path. Declaring an entity does not open a database. The adapter named by Entity.adapter is usually application code. In JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart and Ruby, and in Go, Rust and C# services that run as WebAssembly, the name "indexeddb" needs no adapter code: Tachyon keeps one IndexedDB object store per Table, keyed by the Id field. A Dart, Ruby or WebAssembly service answers the page synchronously, so Tachyon loads its Tables into memory before the services start (at most 10,000 rows per Table), reads from that copy and saves changes to IndexedDB in the background. It builds an index for every field that a Store query compares or orders by, and it adds new indexes by upgrading the database version. It never deletes stored rows: if the Id field changes, it stops with a message. A query that has no usable index reads at most 10,000 rows. AllOrNothing collects the writes and saves them in one IndexedDB transaction. A Store that uses "indexeddb" needs no authorizeEntity, because the data never leaves the browser. It handles the transport, the query parameters and tenancy (keeping the data of each customer apart). authorizeEntity must approve every query. Tac stays client-rendered (the browser builds the page). It uses only public TAC_ configuration, never private Yon credentials.
